references.cited_as: Greenspon J, Williams SB, Young HA, Orkin BA. Thrombosed external hemorrhoids: outcome after conservative or surgical management. Dis Colon Rectum. 2004;47(9):1493-1498. doi:10.1007/s10350-004-0607-y. PMID: 15486746.
references.record_title: Thrombosed external hemorrhoids: outcome after conservative or surgical management.
references.article_type: Journal Article (PubMed); retrospective case series per abstract
references.notes: Added to replace the uncheckable 72-hour excision window and 7 to 10 day resolution claims (formerly NEJM ref). PubMed type Journal Article; described in text as retrospective.

claims.text: Retrospective study of 231 patients with thrombosed external hemorrhoids
claims.quote: Two hundred and thirty-one consecutive patients with thrombosed external hemorrhoids treated from 1990 to 2002 were identified. ... Data were gathered retrospectively.

claims.text: Symptom resolution averaged 24 days conservative vs 3.9 days surgical
claims.quote: Time to symptom resolution averaged 24 days in the conservative group vs. 3.9 days in the surgical group ( P < 0.0001).

claims.text: Recurrence 25.4% conservative vs 6.3% surgical
claims.quote: The rate of recurrence in the conservative group was 25.4 percent (4/29; 14 percent were excised) whereas only 6.3 percent of the surgical patients had recurrence ( P < 0.0001).

claims.text: Most conservatively treated patients experience resolution; excision faster with fewer recurrences
claims.quote: Although most patients treated conservatively will experience resolution of their symptoms, excision of thrombosed external hemorrhoids results in more rapid symptom resolution, lower incidence of recurrence, and longer remission intervals.
